newsitem.title: USA: Obscenities spray-painted on Lincoln's tomb.
newsitem.headline: Obscenities spray-painted on Lincoln's tomb.

text.p: Vandals spray-painted obscenities on the stone base of the building housing former President Abraham Lincoln's tomb, police said Sunday.
Police had no suspects in the painting, which apparently took place Saturday night, Springfield Police Sgt. Ricky Davis said.
Davis would not say whether the graffiti had racial overtones.
Lincoln, the 16th U.S. president, issued the Emancipation Proclamation, freeing the slaves, in 1863.
Southern states, in which slavery was most common, began seceding after Lincoln's election, since he was known to regard slavery as an evil.
He led the nation during its victory in the war with the southern Confederacy, made up of seceding states.
He was elected to a second term in 1864 and was assassinated in 1865.
Lincoln, though born in Kentucky, spent a substantial part of his life in Illinois as a lawyer and legislator in Springfield, the state capitol.
